title: Lazy Mole Sauce
description: A short toast brings cocoa and ancho together in a weeknight mole with no dried chiles to soak.

steps.title: Start the sauce
steps.text: Warm {oil} in the 10-inch HexClad skillet over low heat.

steps.title: Toast gently
steps.text: Gently stir {ancho}, {paprika}, {cumin}, {cinnamon}, {cocoa}, {garlic} and {blackgarlic} in the oil for 20 seconds.

steps.title: Simmer the base
steps.text: Slowly whisk in {broth}, {peanut}, {honey} and {amino}. Simmer for 6 minutes until smooth and fragrant.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Pour the slurry into the simmering sauce while whisking. Bubble gently for 1 minute until it coats a spoon.

steps.title: Finish the sauce
steps.text: Measure into a heatproof jug and adjust with a little hot water to yield 1 cup. Serve over chicken or turkey.

notes: Yield: 1 cup. Low-sodium option for the full batch: reduce coconut aminos to 1.5 g and keep the same final yield. Use unsalted broth throughout. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, omit citrus or vinegar and replace its weight with water. Make ahead: chill in small jars for up to 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes, freeze in quarter-cup portions up to 2 months. Fridge reheat: whisk over low heat to 165°F. Freezer reheat: thaw overnight in the fridge, then reheat as above. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 55 kcal, 1.9 g protein, 5.1 g total carbohydrate, 3.6 g fat, 1.0 g fiber, 36 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 54 kcal, 1.9 g protein, 4.8 g total carbohydrate, 3.6 g fat, 1.0 g fiber, 16 mg sodium.
